# hetznerrobot_boot_windows (Resource)

Activates the Windows installation of a dedicated server; the Windows addon has to be ordered for the server first. **The installation wipes the server.** It starts on the next reboot — pair it with `hetznerrobot_server_reset` — after which Robot reports `active = false`; the resource keeps that as a fact. Only one boot configuration can be active at a time. Destroying the resource deactivates the installation if it is still pending.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Needs the Windows addon ordered for the server; wipes the server on the next reboot.
resource "hetznerrobot_boot_windows" "windows" {
  server_number = 321
  os            = "Windows Server 2022 Standard Edition"
  lang          = "en"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `lang` (String) Language of the installation, e.g. `en`.
- `os` (String) Windows version to install (see `hetznerrobot_boot.windows_os`).
- `server_number` (Number) Server to configure.

### Read-Only

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the configuration is still pending. Robot clears it once the server has booted it.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Root (or Administrator) password Robot generated on activation. Only the activation answer carries it, so it stays as it was after the configuration is used up.
- `server_ip` (String) Main IP address of the server.
- `server_ipv6_net` (String) Main IPv6 net of the server.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Only a pending (still active) activation can be imported.
tofu import hetznerrobot_boot_windows.windows 321
```
